title: The Resistance Fighters of Occupied France in World War II

sentences.text: In 1942, France was under German occupation.
The streets of Paris were filled with soldiers.
People lived in fear.
But not everyone was afraid.
Some were brave.
They were the resistance fighters.
Marie was one of them.
She was a young woman, only 22 years old.
She worked as a nurse by day.
By night, she was a spy.
She passed messages and helped hide people.
Her brother, Pierre, was also in the resistance.
He was a mechanic.
He fixed cars and made weapons for the fighters.
One night, Marie received a message.
It was from Jacques, the leader of their group.
He needed to meet her.
They met in a small café.
Jacques told her about a new mission.
They had to blow up a train.
The train carried supplies for the German army.
It was a dangerous mission, but it was important.
Marie and Pierre prepared for the mission.
They gathered explosives and made a plan.
The night of the mission, they dressed in dark clothes.
They moved quietly through the streets.
They reached the train tracks and placed the explosives.
They set the timer and ran away.
The explosion was loud.
It shook the ground.
The train was destroyed.
The German soldiers were angry.
They searched for the resistance fighters.
Marie and Pierre hid in a safe house.
They stayed there for days.
They knew they had to be careful.
After the mission, Marie continued her work.
She helped many people escape.
She passed messages and gathered information.
She was always careful.
But one day, she was caught.
A German soldier saw her passing a message.
She was arrested and taken to a prison.
In prison, Marie was scared.
But she did not give up.
She knew she had to stay strong.
She thought of her brother and her friends.
She knew they were still fighting.
She hoped they would rescue her.
One night, there was a noise outside her cell.
It was Pierre and Jacques.
They had come to save her.
They fought the guards and opened her cell.
Marie was free.
They ran through the prison and escaped into the night.
Marie and Pierre continued to fight in the resistance.
They never gave up.
They knew their work was important.
They wanted to see France free again.
And in 1944, their dream came true.
The Allies liberated France.
The resistance fighters were heroes.
Marie and Pierre were proud of their work.
They had fought for their country and won.
